title: The Locked Wing
content: Morning entered the archive reluctantly. A thin gray light settled over the reading tables while Mara followed her map toward the eastern wing.
The map ended at a narrow corridor. Beyond it stood a door bound in dark metal, its keyhole covered by a sliding plate. Someone had written CLOSED in chalk across the stone.
Her instructions said nothing about a key. Still, one waited in the pocket of the coat she had worn on the ferry. It was warm when she drew it out.
The lock turned without resistance. Beyond the door, the air smelled of rain and dust, and rows of glass cases reflected a ceiling filled with unfamiliar stars.
Each case held a single book. Most were blank. One contained a neat account of her arrival, down to the captain's unfinished warning and the bell at eleven fifty-nine.
Mara closed it. The next volume opened by itself. Its first page bore tomorrow's date, but the ink below was still moving.
A sound traveled through the floor: three short pulses, then silence, then three more. It was too regular to be the settling of an old building.
She returned the key to her pocket and left the wing unlocked. Behind her, unseen pages began to turn in sequence.
